figures.caption: Structure of AW1 peptide and its membrane-disrupting activities.a–b Predicted secondary structures of AW1 and AW2 by Alphafold2 (a), and their secondary structure in SDS or H2O solutions determined by circular dichroism (b). c Confocal images of AW1 (0–5 × MIC) incubated with K. pneumoniae and S. aureus for 45 min. Viable bacterial cells stained green with SYTO9 whereas dead cells stained red with PI. Quantification of relative fluorescence intensity using Image J software. Scale bars:10 μm. d Time-kill kinetics assay of K. pneumoniae and S. aureus treated with AW1 (0–5 × MIC) for 180 min. Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and polymyxin-B (1 × MIC) were used as negative and positive controls, respectively. e SEM images of K. pneumoniae and S. aureus after 1 h of exposure to AW1 (1 × and 5 × MIC). Scar bars: 3 μm. f, g Membrane property changes of K. pneumoniae and S. aureus following exposure to varying concentration AW1. Membrane fluidity was determined using 10 µM Laurdan (f), membrane depolarization was measured using 0.5 µM DiSC3(5) (g), and polymyxin-B (10 × MIC) as the positive control. h Assessment of the effects of exogenous LPS, LTA, and the four phospholipids (PG, PC, PE, and CL) on AW1’s antibacterial activity using microdilution experiments. MIC changes of AW1 against K. pneumoniae and S. aureus in the presence of varying doses of LPS (0–128 μg/mL), LTAs (0–128 μg/mL), PC, PE, PG, and CL (0–16 μg/mL). i The interaction between AW1 and LPS determined by ITC assay, where 0.05 mM LPS was titrated into 0.5 mM AW1 in HEPES buffer at 25 °C. Experiments in (c–i) are presented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) from three biologically independent experiments. One-way ANOVA, followed by Tukey’s multiple comparison test f. P values are indicated in the graph. Source data are provided in this paper.
figures.label: Fig. 1

figures.caption: AW2 significantly enhances the antimicrobial activity of AW1.a, b Growth conditions of K. pneumoniae and S. aureus after exposure to AW1 (1 × MIC) and AW2 (0-50 μM) individually or in combination for 18 h (a). Identification and marking of a single colony in green using a colony counting and measurement instrument. The growth density of bacteria was determined at 600 nm after exposure to peptides for 18 h (b). (n = 4 for each condition). c Checkerboard broth microdilution assays comparing the antimicrobial activity of AW1 (1/4 -16 ×MIC) and AW2 (0–50 μM) against K. pneumoniae and S. aureus. Dark-red regions represent higher bacterial densities and lower inhibition rates of the combination treatment. FIC refers to the minimum concentrations of AW1 and AW2 required for relative bacterial growth density to remain below 10%. Synergy was defined as an FIC index of ≤ 0.5. d DLS intensity spectra of AW1, AW2, and 1:1 AW1/AW2 mixture. The total AMP concentration was 10 μM for each case. e, f Transcriptome gene expression (e) and volcano plot of annotated genes (f) in K. pneumoniae after exposure to AW1 (1 × MIC) or a combination of AW2 (25 μM) for 2 h. The x- and y-axes in the volcano plot represent the magnitude of the expression changes and the corresponding statistical significance, respectively. The threshold for identifying significant DEGs was set at p-value < 0.05, and |log2 Fold change| ≥1. g, h The most significant gene ontology (GO) (g) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) (h) enrichment analyses displaying the effect of adding AW2 in K. pneumoniae. The significance cutoff was set at a q-value < 0.05. Enriched pathways were selected based on the number of significant genes, prioritizing those with higher counts. Distinctive genes were categorized based on their functional similarities. Significant differences using an unpaired Student’s t test (two-tailed). Experiments in (b) are presented as means ± S.D. P values are indicated in the graph (b). Source data are provided in this paper.
figures.label: Fig. 2

figures.caption: Synergistic antimicrobial activity of AW1 and AW2 against local S. aureus skin infection in mice.a Flowchart depicting the BALB/c mouse skin infection model (7-week-old female, n = 8 per group). Mice with a symmetrical curved wound (10 mm in diameter) on the dorsal surface after anesthesia were inoculated with S. aureus (107 CFU/mL). Treatment groups were administered 50 μL of AW1 (2 mg/kg), AW2 (2 mg/kg) individually or in combination, vancomycin (2 mg/kg), or PBS (0.05 mM) at three 24-hour intervals. Changes in ulcer size were monitored over time (72-144 h), and the physiological parameters of ulcers were evaluated at specific time points. b–c, Representative photographs of the symmetrical elliptical wound (b). Quantification of specific changes in the wound area using Image J software at three-day intervals (c). ‘Sham’ refers to the sham surgery group, while ‘Vehicle’ represents the solvent group. d, e The bacterial quantification (d) and ELISA-based anti-inflammatory activity assay (e) of the ulcer after three rounds of peptide treatment. Scale bars: 1 cm. Eight biologically independent experiments were performed in (b–e). Significant differences using an unpaired Student’s t test (two tailed). Experiments in (c) are presented as means ± S.D. One-way ANOVA, followed by Tukey’s multiple comparison test. P values are indicated in the graphs (c, d, e). Box-and-whisker plots represent the minimum, first-quartile, median, third-quartile, and maximum values. Source data are provided in this paper.
figures.label: Fig. 3

figures.caption: Combination of AW1 and AW2 effectively reduces bacterial resistance and biofilm formation.a Selected drug resistance genes with a significant cutoff set at a p-value < 0.05 and |log2 Fold change| ≥1. b The development of resistance assay in K. pneumoniae and S. aureus in vitro induced by AW1 (1 × MIC) AW2 (25 μM) or combined together. Two antibiotics with distinct mechanisms were used as positive controls. c, d Biofilm formation prevention by AW1 (1 × MIC) and AW2 (25 μM) or their combinations assessed using crystal violet staining (c) and 2,3,5-Triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) assays (d). Culturing K. pneumoniae (red lines, gray columns) and S. aureus (blue lines and columns) for 48 h prior to AMP administration, or co-incubation of bacteria and peptides for 24 h enabled evaluation of peptide efficacy in eradicating established biofilms and assessment of their inhibitory effects on biofilm formation, respectively (n = 3 for each condition). e Representative photographs of crystal violet staining and TTC assays. An enhanced color response indicates the superior synergistic antibiofilm effect of AW1 and AW2. f Bactericidal activity of AW1 (1 × MIC), AW2 (25 μM) or their combinations against K. pneumoniae and S. aureus cells in established biofilms. Viable bacteria were quantified on MH plates after a 2-h exposure of pre-cultured 24-h biofilms to peptides (n = 6). g Bactericidal efficacy of AW1 (1 × MIC), AW2 (25 μM), or their combinations against persister cells derived from biofilms. The biofilms formed by K. pneumoniae and S. aureus were exposed to rifampicin (100 × MIC) for 24 h. The persister cell count was determined by incubating the cells with the peptide for 2 h (n = 8). Significant differences using an unpaired Student’s t test (two-tailed) are represented. Experiments in c, f, and g are presented as means± S.D. P values are indicated in the graph (d, f, g). Source data are provided in this paper.
figures.label: Fig. 4

figures.caption: AW1 contributes to the synergistic disruption of the outer membrane and intracellular absorption of AW2 in bacteria.a Selected membrane expression genes with a significant cutoff (p-value < 0.05 and |log2 Fold change | ≥1) in K. pneumoniae. b, c Penetration of bacterial cell membranes by AW1 (5 × MIC) and AW2 (5–50 μM) determined using PI (10 μM) (b). The synergistic effect of both peptides on the outer membrane of K. pneumoniae and E. coli (c) was measured by NPN (10 μM)(n = 5). d–f The uptake of peptides by bacterial cell membranes assessed by fluorescence intensity (d), confocal laser scanning (e) and flow cytometry assays (f). The bacterial strains of K. pneumoniae and S. aureus treated with fluorescently tagged AW2 (FITC-labeled, 25 μM) alone or in combination with AW1 (1-2 × MIC), using trypan blue-induced extracellular fluorescence burst assay (n = 3). Scar bars: 10 μm. g Schematic illustration depicting the differential impact of AW1 and AW2 on the cell membranes of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. AW1 demonstrates disruptive effects on bacterial outer and inner membranes, whereas AW2 solely induces sensitivity towards the outer membrane. Combining these two peptides generates a synergistic membrane-disrupting effect. Data in the experiments (b–f) are presented as mean ± S.D. One-way ANOVA, followed by Tukey’s multiple comparison test. P values are indicated in the graphs (b, c, and d). Source data are provided in this paper.
figures.label: Fig. 5

figures.caption: Interaction between AW2 and DNA and its inhibitory effects on bacterial transcription and translation.a Downregulation of selected DNA repair and replication genes in K. pneumoniae. The significance cutoff was set at p-value < 0.05 and |log2 Fold change| ≥ 1. b–d The binding capacity of AW1 (0–50 μM) or AW2 (0–50 μM) with E. coli genomic DNA (10 μg/mL) assessed by gel retardation experiments (b), UV-visible spectroscopy (c), and fluorescence intensity of EB solution (1.5 μg/mL) (d). Ultraviolet spectral assays were conducted over a wavelength range of 240–320 nm. Fluorescence spectra were recorded from 575 to 800 nm (Ex = 535 nm) for EB competitive binding assays. The sampling interval was set to 5 nm. e–i Molecular dynamic simulation results showing the interaction of AW1 and AW2 with CpG ODN including snapshots (e), peptide helicity of AW1 and AW2 over time (f), probability distributions of contact number between AW1/AW2 and DNA (g), number of hydrogen bonds between AW1/AW2 and DNA as a function of simulation time (h), and potential of mean forces for AW1/AW2 to dissociate from DNA (i). j Fluorescence intensity of EGFP protein produced by the recombinant plasmid vectors plevx2.4c under in vitro transcription-translation conditions. k Photographic documentation of products generated from in vitro transcription/translation SDS-PAGE. The molecular weight of the EGFP protein is approximately 26.7 kDa. Band intensities within the 25–35 kDa protein marker range reflect EGFP expression levels. Data in the experiments (b–k) are presented as the mean ± S.D, based on three biologically independent experiments. One-way ANOVA, followed by Tukey’s multiple comparison test. P values are indicated in the graph (j). Source data are provided in this paper.
figures.label: Fig. 6

figures.caption: AW1 and AW2 induce bacterial oxidative stress associated with the antimicrobial activity of both peptides.a Selected oxidative stress genes in K. pneumoniae with a significant cutoff set at p-value < 0.05, and |log2 Fold change| ≥ 1. b–c Levels of NADPH (b) in K. pneumoniae and S. aureus, and FAD (c) in E. coli, following exposure to the combination of AW1 (1 × MIC) and AW2 (25 μM). d The oxidoreductase activity of K. pneumoniae and S. aureus, including SOD, CAT, and GPx, following treatment with a combination of AW1 (1 × MIC) and AW2 (25 μM), either individually or in combination. e, f Assessment of ROS levels (e) and lipid peroxidation (f) in K. pneumoniae and S. aureus after exposure to AW1 (1 × MIC) and AW2 (25 μM). The antioxidants thiourea (Tu, 300 mM), N-acetylcysteine (NAC, 10 mM), 2,2-Dipyridyl (DP, 75 μM), and polymyxin B (5 × MIC) were included in the study. g Intracellular ATP production in K. pneumoniae and S. aureus after exposure to the combination treatment of AW1 (1 × MIC) and AW2 (25 μM). h Confocal laser scanning images showing distinct ROS, •OH, and O2•– (green) or H2O2 (red). The combined treatment of AW1 and AW2, at a concentration equivalent to (e). Scar bars: 10 μm. i Spot titer assays of K. pneumoniae and S. aureus incubated with AW1 (1 × MIC) or supplemented with AW2 (25 μM) for 18 h. j The bacterial intensity of K. pneumoniae and S. aureus incubated with the combination of AW1 (5 × MIC) and AW2 (25 μM), along with the antioxidant Tu (300 mM) or NAC (10 mM) for 18 h. k Schematic illustration depicting bacterial oxidative stress induced by AW1 and AW2. The red background indicates the presence of ROS, whereas the gray background represents inhibition. Data in the experiments (b–j) are presented as mean ± S.D, based on three biologically independent experiments. One-way ANOVA, followed by Tukey’s multiple comparison test. P values are indicated in the graphs (b–g, j). Source data are provided in this paper.

figures.caption: Effective synergistic antibacterial effects of AMPs and NDACPs in different animal species.a–f, Spot titer assays were conducted using NDACPs (25 μM), and AMPs (1 × MIC), including PN-1 and PN-2 from Pelophlax nigromaculata (a), OL-2 and OL-1 from Odorrana livida (b), RC-1 and RC-2 from Rana catesbeiana (c), AS-4 and AS-2 from Alligator sinensis (d), PS-1 and PS-4 from Pelodiscus sinensis (e), and LL-37 and H2A from Homo sapiens (f).
